messages:
alex: FYI Moneta Capital signed NDA and wants a 3-week technical POC to replace CompetitorY. Primary ask: make their transaction-summary API behave the same. Need plan for shim, parity tests, security checklist, and a short pricing bridge.

priya: I'll own the prompt parity work. Suggest we capture 1k representative customer queries (anonymized) and run them through both endpoints to catalog drift.

tom: For the shim, simplest approach is an adapter that accepts CompetitorY JSON and emits Redwood batch requests. Important differences: CompetitorY uses `maxTokens` and `stopSequences[]` and returns `text` string; our API uses `max_output_tokens`, `stop` single string, and returns `outputs` array. Adapter should normalize both directions.

nina: Security: they require KMS-backed key management and proof of encryption-at-rest + VPC peering for POC. We can provision a Private deployment in eu-west-1 for data residency. I'll prep SOC2, encryption whitepaper, and a short VPC peering runbook.

alex: Timeline proposal: week0 prep + infra; week1 run 1k parity tests; week2 iterate shims and prompts; week3 run final validation and handoff.

priya: Technical note: CompetitorY's tokenizer splits emojis differently and their default temp is 0.6. Recommend running with Redwood equivalent model and temp settings and then adding canonicalization steps (strip trailing punctuation, normalize unicode) before diffing.

platform-bot: eu-west-1 available GPUs: 4. Private deployment slots free: 1.

tom: Example adapter snippet to show them in the POC kickoff deck:
```json
// CompetitorY request
{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"{{input}}"}],"maxTokens":120,"stopSequences":["\n\n"]}
// Adapter -> Redwood
{"model":"redwood-2b","input":"{{input}}","max_output_tokens":120,"stop":"\n\n"}
```
And response mapping: our `outputs` -> join into single `text` field.

priya: For automated parity scoring: use embedding cosine (flag <0.9), normalized edit distance for short outputs, and a human review pass for top 250 business-critical prompts. Also track failure modes (hallucination, redaction differences).

alex: Procurement wants a 60-day price match window if we underdeliver. Sales suggests offering a promotional bridge: match CompetitorY effective per-call price for first 2M calls or a 3-month discounted committed capacity for Dedicated. Thoughts?

sales-bot: Suggested offer template: "Bridge: match effective per-call price for first 2M calls OR 3 months Dedicated at 20% off + engineering parity retainer (optional)".

nina: Legal flagged two enterprise blockers: (1) they require a data deletion guarantee for training exclusion; (2) they asked if we provide logging redaction for PCI/PII. We can commit to POC-only retention and run DLP redaction pipeline, but training-exclusion needs legal sign-off.

priya: Determinism question: we cannot guarantee bitwise identical outputs across different models. We can offer low-temperature configs to reduce variance and deterministic post-processing in the shim (canonical punctuation, whitespace trim).

platform-bot: Reservation request #PR-773 queued for Private eu-west-1.

tom: Latency note: CompetitorY's average p50 is ~120ms. Our continuous batching means p50 can vary; we can tune max_batch_latency_ms and batch_size to hit ~120ms at 200 qps. There will be tradeoffs with cost.

alex: Can someone draft the short answers for the RFP security questions this afternoon? Need to include SOC2, KMS, VPC peering steps, and our retention policy for POC.

nina: I'll draft. Also will attach a sample KMS integration snippet and a one-page data-flow diagram.

priya: Who can produce the anonymized 1k prompt set? We need to mask emails, account numbers, and any payment fields. I can run DLP rules, but need eng-sre to whitelist this export.
tom: I can do the export and co-run the DLP. We'll keep everything in the Private infra bucket.

alex: Meeting with Moneta Tue 11am. Who's presenting?

priya: I'll present parity methodology and sample diffs.
tom: I'll demo the shim and the adapter code + show live diff for 10 prompts.
nina: I'll handle security and compliance questions.

alex: Great. Action items: tom - build adapter PoC + example payloads; priya - assemble 1k anonymized prompts and parity scripts; nina - security packet + KMS runbook; sales - prepare bridge offer and contract stub. We'll update the shared runbook by EOD Monday.

sales-bot: Runbook created: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/moneta-compat-poc

alex: Thanks team. Keep updates here. :white_check_mark:
